newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Strike-threat truckers to meet Colombia gov't rep.
newsitem.headline: Strike-threat truckers to meet Colombia gov't rep.

text.p: The leader of Colombia's largest truck drivers' organization said he would meet with Transport Ministry officials at 1400 local time/ 1900 GMT Tuesday in a bid to avert a new nationwide strike.

Javier Suarez, chairman of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC which represents about 85 percent of the country's truckers, said the meeting would take place in the Caribbean port city of Cartagena with regional ministry representatives.
The immediate aim of the talks is to solve the dispute in Cartagena, where truckers have been on strike since Monday.
But Suarez said failure to reach an accord there could spark a nationwide stoppage.

"Undoubtedly this stoppage could spread...but the last thing we want is to create another general trauma for the nation but it is up to the Transport Ministry to crack the whip and make sure the transport companies observe the previous agreement," Suarez told Reuters by phone.
"We will be taking a decision on whether to launch a new nationwide strike in the course of the week depending on the outcome of today's talks," he added.
The ACC declared an "amber alert" Tuesday in protest at what it said was transport companies' continued failure to observe a government-brokered accord that ended two previous strikes.
The terms of the deal included a 30 percent hike in freight rates, payments for waiting time and a revision of vehicle licensing taxes and regulations regarding the age of vehicles.

The most recent stoppage, which lasted from April 20 through April 25, brought almost all transport operations to a standstill. It delayed the shipment of at least 200,000 60-kg bags of key coffee exports, sugar and coal, according to industry officials.
